mainTopic: טומאה הותרה בציבור vs. טומאה דחויה בציבור: whether a communal offering may be brought in טומאה even when a pure alternative is available
overview: This עמוד continues the מחלוקת between רב נחמן, who holds טומאה הותרה בציבור (impurity is fully permitted for public offerings), and רב ששת, who holds טומאה דחויה בציבור (impurity is only pushed aside, so purity is still sought when possible). רב ששת brings a ברייתא showing that an impure מנחת העומר is replaced if another is available. רב נחמן answers that this is only because the עומר has שיריים that must be eaten in purity. The גמרא challenges him with a ברייתא about the מנחה of bulls, rams, and sheep, which seem to be the סוכות offerings. רב נחמן reads them as the פר עבודה זרה (no fixed time), אילו של אהרן (an individual's offering), and the כבש of the עומר (has leftovers). A ברייתא about impure blood sprinkled on purpose is limited to an individual's offering. A ברייתא saying the ציץ brings acceptance even for public offerings is answered in two ways: it means only the individual's offering, or only public offerings without a fixed time. The עמוד ends with a new challenge from the verse about the ציץ, which begins eliminating פיגול and נותר and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reason: corpse impurity is permitted for the public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining רב נחמן's view: the תורה fully permits טומאת מת in public offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the תורה permits all corpse-impurity in matters of the public.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the reason for רב נחמן's view, which began on the previous עמוד. Even impure כהנים may serve, because the תורה permitted טומאת מת for the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that טומאה הותרה בציבור. 'הותרה' means fully permitted, not just pushed aside. So there is no need to search for pure כהנים or pure items, because impurity is simply not a problem for a קרבן ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity that comes from contact with a dead body
The public, the community; here, communal offerings
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה
Permitted it

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a thought. The 'דְּ' (for/because) connects it to רב נחמן's opinion from the previous עמוד. It is his reason, not a new statement.

phrases.english: For all corpse-impurity in matters of the public
phrases.notes: This wraps up the reason behind רב נחמן's view.

phrases.english: the Merciful One (the Torah) permitted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכֹל טוּמְאַת מֵת בְּצִיבּוּר רַחֲמָנָא שַׁרְיַיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב נחמן's position from the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טומאת מת is fully permitted for public offerings (הותרה), so no effort is needed to find purity.

steps.title: רב ששת brings a ברייתא about the עומר offering
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת cites a ברייתא. If the מנחת העומר becomes impure in the כהן's hand, they bring a replacement. Only if there is no other one, the כהן stays quiet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: How do I know my view? Because a ברייתא teaches: If a כהן was offering the מנחת העומר and it became impure in his hand, he announces it, and they bring another one in its place. If that is the only one there, they tell him: 'Be smart and keep quiet.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a source to support his view that impurity is only דחויה. He is setting up the proof. He will point to the exact words in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר is a קרבן ציבור. Yet the ברייתא says that if it becomes impure, they replace it with a pure one when they can. They use the impure one only when there is no other option. That is how something behaves when it is only 'pushed aside', not fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (introducing one's source)
The barley meal-offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, a communal offering
It became impure in his hand
Be clever and stay silent
In its place

steps.whyThisMatters: The 'keep quiet' clause shows that an impure עומר can still be used in the end, because the ציבור rule allows it. The question is only whether we must look for a pure one first.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
From where do I say it?
For it was taught in a baraita:
If he was standing and offering the Omer meal-offering
and it became impure in his hand,
he says so, and they bring another in its place.
And if there is none there except it,
they say to him:
Be smart and keep quiet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source against רב נחמן's view and in support of רב ששת's
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that טומאה דחויה בציבור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the מנחת העומר becoming impure

steps.title: Pinpointing the proof: they bring a replacement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the key words of the proof: 'he announces it and they bring another in its place.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it teaches: 'He announces it, and they bring another in its place!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zeroes in on the exact words that prove רב ששת's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If impurity were fully permitted for the ציבור, there would be no reason to replace an impure עומר. Since the ברייתא requires a replacement when one is available, purity is still preferred. So impurity is only דחויה.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case it teaches (pointing to the decisive words)
Pushed aside, only overridden when necessary

phrases.english: In any case it teaches:
'He says so, and they bring another in its place!'

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת אוֹמֵר וּמְבִיאִין אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the specific inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 2
steps.raayaObject: Purity must be sought for a קרבן ציבור when possible
steps.raayaSupportSource: The clause 'ומביאין אחרת תחתיה' in the ברייתא

steps.title: רב נחמן: purity is preferred only where leftovers are eaten
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן agrees that purity is preferred when the offering has שיריים that will be eaten. The עומר is such a case, so it does not disprove his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: I agree in a case where there are leftovers to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on רב ששת's proof. He limits the ברייתא to offerings that have parts to be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר has שיריים that the כהנים eat, and the eating is not permitted in טומאה. That is why we try to bring a pure one. For the offering on the מזבח itself, טומאה is still fully הותרה. So the ברייתא does not contradict רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: I agree / I concede
Remnants of a מנחה left over after the קמיצה, eaten by כהנים
For eating

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not giving up his view. He agrees only about the eating part. The offering itself on the מזבח may still be brought in טומאה.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
I agree
where there are remnants to be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מוֹדֵינָא הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא שִׁירַיִים לַאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 2-3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the ברייתא to offerings that have edible leftovers
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the replacement was required because of the offering itself. It may instead be required because of the eating of the שיריים.

steps.title: Challenge from the meal-offering of bulls, rams, and sheep
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא about מנחת נסכים, which is fully burned and has no leftovers. Yet it says they still bring a replacement.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If he was offering the meal-offering of bulls, rams, and sheep, and it became impure in his hand, he announces it, and they bring another in its place. If that is the only one there, they tell him: 'Be smart and keep quiet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty against רב נחמן's answer from step 4. It quotes a source about a מנחה that has nothing to eat, yet it still needs a pure replacement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנחת נסכים that comes with bulls, rams, and sheep is burned entirely on the מזבח. It has no שיריים to eat. If the ברייתא still requires a replacement, then the reason cannot be about eating. The next step completes the challenge by arguing that these must be the public offerings of סוכות. Only then does the ברייתא clash with רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a תנאי source)
The מנחת נסכים brought with these animals, burned entirely

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this מנחה with the עומר. The whole point of the challenge is that this מנחה is completely burned and has no part to eat.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מַקְרִיב מִנְחַת פָּרִים וְאֵילִים וּכְבָשִׂים,
phrases.english: If he was offering the meal-offering of bulls, rams, and sheep,
and it became impure in his hand,
he says so, and they bring another in its place.
And if there is none there except it,
they say to him:
Be smart and keep quiet.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הָיָה מַקְרִיב מִנְחַת פָּרִים וְאֵילִים וּכְבָשִׂים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's answer from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that purity is preferred only where there are שיריים to eat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנחת נסכים has no edible leftovers, yet the ברייתא still requires a pure replacement. So the preference for purity cannot depend on eating.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת proves from the עומר that purity is sought even for public offerings. רב נחמן answers that this is only because of the eating. The גמרא then challenges him with a fully burned מנחה that still needs a replacement.

steps.title: The replacement rule seems to apply to the holiday offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens its challenge: the bulls, rams, and sheep in the ברייתא must be the communal offerings of חג (סוכות), and those are exactly where רב נחמן says טומאה is fully permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא talking about the bulls, rams, and sheep brought on the holiday of סוכות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its attack from Step 5. It argues that the ברייתא's bulls, rams, and sheep must be the public offerings of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offerings of סוכות are public and have a fixed time, so they are the clearest example of where רב נחמן says טומאה is fully permitted. Their מנחת נסכים is fully burned and has no leftovers to eat. If the ברייתא still says to bring a pure replacement, then purity is required even here, and that goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Isn't it...?' This introduces the reading the questioner thinks is the obvious one.
The Festival. Here it means סוכות, when many bulls, rams, and sheep are offered.
Bulls, rams, and sheep, the animals whose offerings come with a מנחת נסכים.

phrases.english: What, is it not
the bulls, rams, and sheep of the Festival!
phrases.notes: These are the public offerings of סוכות, which come at a fixed time.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו, פָּרִים אֵילִים וּכְבָשִׂים דְּחַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in Step 5 by naming which offerings the ברייתא must mean.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that טומאה is fully permitted (הותרה) for public offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires a pure replacement for the offerings of סוכות. These are public, fixed-time offerings with no leftovers, so purity is still preferred even where רב נחמן says it should not matter.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains the bulls, rams, and sheep as special cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains each animal in the ברייתא as a case outside his rule. The bull is the פר עבודה זרה, which has no fixed time. The ram is אילו של אהרן, which belongs to an individual. The sheep is the כבש of the עומר, which has leftovers that are eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן would answer: No. The 'bulls' means the bull brought for public idol worship. Even though it is a public offering, it has no fixed time, so we look for a pure replacement. The 'rams' means אהרן's ram on יום כיפור. Even though it has a fixed time, it is an individual's offering, so we look for a pure replacement. The 'sheep' means the sheep brought with the עומר, where there are leftovers to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the challenge. He says the ברייתא is not talking about the סוכות offerings at all, but about three special offerings where purity really is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer shows the exact limits of רב נחמן's rule. טומאה is fully permitted only for an offering that is public, has a fixed time, and has no leftovers to eat. Each animal in the ברייתא is missing one of these three conditions, so a pure replacement makes sense, and his view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull the community brings if it mistakenly worshipped idols.
It has a fixed time set for it.
We look for (a pure replacement).
The ram of אהרן, the כהן גדול's own offering on יום כיפור.
Leftovers that are meant to be eaten.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, טומאה is fully permitted only when all three conditions are met: (1) a public offering, (2) with a fixed time, (3) with no leftovers to eat.
steps.confusionAlert: אילו של אהרן is offered on יום כיפור, a fixed day, but it still does not count as public. It belongs to the כהן גדול as an individual, so the fixed time alone is not enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer turns 'public offering' into three exact conditions. Later stages of the sugya rely on these conditions.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman could say to you: No:
'bulls' means the bull for idolatry,
even though it is a public offering,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא קְבִיעַ לֵיהּ זְמַן — מַהְדְּרִינַן.
phrases.english: since it has no fixed time, we look for a pure replacement.
phrases.notes: This offering misses one of the conditions: it has no fixed time.

phrases.english: 'rams' means the ram of Aaron,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דִּקְבִיעַ לֵיהּ זְמַן,
phrases.english: which, even though it has a fixed time,
since it belongs to an individual, we look for a pure replacement.
phrases.notes: This offering misses one of the conditions: it isn't public.

phrases.english: 'sheep' means the sheep that comes with the omer,
where there are leftovers to be eaten.
phrases.notes: This one misses a condition too, since it does have leftovers to eat. It's the same reason given in Step 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 5–6 by reading the ברייתא as speaking about other offerings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which cases the ברייתא is talking about (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bulls, rams, and sheep are the public, fixed-time offerings of סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are three special offerings. Each lacks one condition for full permission of טומאה: a fixed time, being public, or having no leftovers.

steps.title: Challenge from impure blood sprinkled on purpose
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if impure blood was sprinkled by mistake the offering is accepted, but if it was sprinkled on purpose it is not. This suggests טומאה is still a real problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If blood became impure and the כהן sprinkled it, then if he did it by mistake, the offering is accepted. If he did it on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן. It says that sprinkling impure blood on purpose makes the offering not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not separate public offerings from private ones. If טומאה were fully permitted for the public, sprinkling impure blood on purpose should be fine there too. So the ruling seems to show that טומאה is still a problem even for public offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They challenged.' A strong challenge from a תנאי source.
He sprinkled it (the blood on the מזבח).
By mistake, without intending to.
On purpose, knowingly.
It was accepted. The offering counts.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
blood that became impure and he sprinkled it,
if by mistake, it is accepted;
if on purpose, it is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a new challenge comes from a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that טומאה is fully permitted for public offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes no exception for public offerings. If impure blood sprinkled on purpose is not accepted, then טומאה is still forbidden and not fully permitted.

steps.title: That ruling is about an individual's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers briefly: the ברייתא about impure blood is talking about an individual's offering. There, טומאה is certainly still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about an individual's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge in one line. That ברייתא only deals with private offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן never said טומאה is permitted for an individual's offering. Once the ברייתא is limited to a יחיד, it says nothing about public offerings, so his view is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When that one was taught...' This limits a source to a specific case.
An individual. Here, an offering brought by one person.

phrases.english: When that was taught, it was about an individual's offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by limiting its ברייתא to individual offerings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling about impure blood applies to all offerings, public ones included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling applies only to an individual's offering, which רב נחמן agrees requires purity.

steps.title: Why would the ציץ be needed for public offerings?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the ציץ makes impure blood, meat, and fats acceptable, including for public offerings. If טומאה were fully permitted for the public, the ציץ would not be needed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: For what does the ציץ bring acceptance? For blood, meat, and fats that became impure. This is true whether by mistake or on purpose, whether forced or willingly, and whether for an individual or for the public. Now if you think טומאה is fully permitted for the public, why do I need the ציץ to bring acceptance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא against רב נחמן. It says the ציץ fixes impure offerings even for the public, which suggests the public's טומאה needs fixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ only fixes something that is a problem. This ברייתא clearly includes public offerings (בין בציבור). If טומאה were fully permitted there, nothing would need fixing. So the ברייתא seems to show that טומאה is only pushed aside (דחויה) for the public, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear.' This introduces a source brought as proof or challenge.
The gold plate on the כהן גדול's forehead. It makes certain impure offerings acceptable.
Brings acceptance. It makes the offering count.
By force, through circumstances out of one's control.
'It enters your mind.' 'If you were to think...'
Fully permitted. No prohibition at all.

steps.confusionAlert: The ציץ does not make the טומאה disappear. It makes an impure offering acceptable after the fact. That is exactly why the גמרא asks: if טומאה is fully permitted for the public, what is there for the ציץ to accept?
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the clearest test so far of הותרה (fully permitted) versus דחויה (only pushed aside). A rule that 'fixes' something only makes sense if there is a problem to fix.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For what does the frontplate bring acceptance?
For the blood and for the meat
and for the fat that became impure,
whether by mistake or on purpose,
whether by force or willingly,
whether for an individual or for the public.
phrases.notes: This is the key phrase. The public is clearly included.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that impurity is fully permitted for the public,
why do I need it to bring acceptance?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עַל מָה הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 9 deflected the blood challenge by limiting it to a יחיד, a new ברייתא is brought that explicitly mentions public offerings (בין בציבור). This makes that kind of deflection look harder.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that טומאה is fully permitted (הותרה) for public offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ציץ fixes only real problems. The ברייתא says the ציץ works for public offerings, so טומאה must still be a problem there. That means it is דחויה, not הותרה.

steps.title: The ציץ is only needed for an individual's offering
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that when the ברייתא says the ציץ makes the offering acceptable, it means only the individual's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן could say to you: when the ברייתא teaches 'the ציץ makes it acceptable,' it is talking about an individual's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10. It says the ציץ's power in that ברייתא applies only to a private person's offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the ציץ was needed for public offerings too, which would show that טומאה is still a problem there. רב נחמן reads the line 'the ציץ makes it acceptable' as referring only to the individual's offering. Public offerings appear in the ברייתא only because they are also valid when brought in טומאה. Their reason is different: טומאה is fully permitted for them.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden plate on the forehead of the כהן גדול. It makes certain impure offerings acceptable.
Makes acceptable, so the offering counts
An individual, meaning a private person's offering

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman could say to you:
When it teaches 'the frontplate effects acceptance'
it refers to an individual's offering.
phrases.notes: The public offering is mentioned only because it is also valid in טומאה, for a different reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the ציץ ברייתא in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא's phrase to individual offerings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ציץ's acceptance applies to every item listed, including public offerings, so טומאה is still a problem for the public.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציץ is needed only for an individual's offering. Public offerings are valid because טומאה is fully permitted for them.

steps.title: Even for the public, only offerings without a fixed time
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even if the ציץ works for public offerings, it is only for those with no fixed time, which are outside רב נחמן's rule anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you wish, say: even if you say it applies to the public, it is only for those offerings that have no fixed time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, alternative answer to the same challenge. It agrees the ציץ may help public offerings, but only the kind that have no set time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's rule that טומאה is permitted covers only public offerings with a fixed time. This is the same idea used in Step 7 for the פר עבודה זרה. So public offerings without a fixed time still need the ציץ, and the ברייתא fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Or if you wish, say. This introduces a second answer.
The community, meaning public offerings
Has a fixed time for being offered

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
even if you say it refers to a communal offering,
it is for those that lack a fixed time.

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's rule that טומאה is fully permitted applies only to public offerings with a fixed time. Individual offerings and public offerings without a fixed time still need the ציץ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, alternative answer to the same קשיא from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to public offerings outside the rule (no fixed time)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the ציץ helps public offerings, טומאה must not be fully permitted for the public.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציץ helps only public offerings without a fixed time, which רב נחמן never included in his rule.

steps.title: Which sin does the ציץ forgive? Ruling out פיגול and נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the verse 'and אהרן will carry the sin of the holy things.' It begins asking which sin the ציץ forgives, and rules out פיגול and נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'And אהרן shall carry the sin of the holy things.' Which sin does he carry? If it is the sin of פיגול, it already says 'it shall not be accepted.' And if it is the sin of נותר, it already says 'it shall not be credited.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against רב נחמן. It quotes a ברייתא that works through options to find which sin the ציץ forgives. The ending of this ברייתא, and the real point of the challenge, comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses elimination. פיגול cannot be the sin, because the תורה says outright that a פיגול offering is never accepted. נותר cannot be it either, because the תורה says it is not credited. This sets up the conclusion that the sin must be טומאה, which will be used against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection from a תנאי source
And אהרן will carry the sin of the holy things. This is the verse about the ציץ.
An offering made invalid by intending to eat or offer it outside its proper time
Sacrificial meat left over past its permitted time

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the full challenge yet. The ברייתא keeps going on the next עמוד. Here it only removes the options that do not work.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'And Aaron will carry the sin of the sacred things,'
and which sin does he carry?
If it is the sin of piggul,
it was already stated: 'It shall not be accepted.'
And if it is the sin of notar,
it was already stated: 'It shall not be credited.'
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new objection against רב נחמן after his two answers to the ציץ ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that טומאה is fully permitted for public offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By eliminating פיגול and נותר, the ברייתא is moving toward showing that the ציץ forgives the sin of טומאה. This will show that טומאה is still a sin that needs forgiveness, and the full challenge comes on the next עמוד.
